VERDICT: DISAGREE. The shipped BEHAVIOUR is, as far as I could measure, correct -- my objections are to two regression guards that do not guard what they say they guard, and to one silent-failure representation. I state that distinction plainly because it decides how small the remedy is.

F1 (BLOCKING under this repo's mutation-probe standard; reproduced). The test that claims to pin commit 8630a36's fix does not exercise the code that fix changed. 8630a36 moved TWO NOTICE prints in `_api` from stdout to stderr, and tests/test_auto_queue.py:244 test_emit_find_prs_unresolved_prints_empty_prs_and_does_not_fail says in its own docstring: "This also pins the fix for a real defect: `_api` and `emit_find_prs` used to print their `NOTICE: ...` diagnostics to stdout". It does not pin `_api` at all -- it monkeypatches resolve_pr_numbers to return None, so `_api` is never called. PROBE: I reverted `_api`'s first NOTICE to stdout (exactly the pre-8630a36 line) and ran tests/test_auto_queue.py: 22 passed, 0 failed. The guard is vacuous for half of what it names. I then reproduced the consequence directly, driving emit_find_prs down the real path with `_run` stubbed to a failing `gh`: at this head stdout is exactly 'prs=\n' and both NOTICEs go to stderr; with the one line reverted, stdout becomes 'NOTICE: gh api .../commits/deadbeef/pulls exited 1: gh: command not found\nprs=\n', whose first line contains no '=' -- precisely the malformed-$GITHUB_OUTPUT failure the docstring describes. Remedy is a few lines: one test that stubs `_run`/`_api` to fail and asserts stdout is exactly ['prs=']. This matters here specifically because this repository has shipped a test written to catch vacuous checks that was itself vacuous; a docstring asserting coverage it does not have is the same shape.

F2 (BLOCKING under the same standard; reproduced). tests/test_auto_queue.py:133 test_resolve_pr_numbers_from_workflow_run_uses_head_sha_not_pull_requests cannot detect the code trusting `workflow_run.pull_requests`. It seeds `"pull_requests": []` -- empty -- so "ignored the field" and "read the field and found it empty" are indistinguishable, and its own assertion message gives this away: "must resolve from the head sha, not trust the EMPTY pull_requests list". Its docstring says the field "must never be read". PROBE: I changed the resolution line to `pulls = workflow_run.get("pull_requests") or _api(...)`, i.e. trust the field whenever it is non-empty -- the exact behaviour the PR body promises it does not have. All 22 tests passed. The same empty-list seeding appears in test_resolve_pr_numbers_from_workflow_run_excludes_closed_and_wrong_base. Remedy: seed `pull_requests` with a NON-EMPTY wrong value (e.g. [{"number": 999}]) and assert the result comes from `commits/{sha}/pulls` regardless.

F3 (BLOCKING, reproduced -- this is this repository's signature defect, relocated into the new resolution layer). An unresolved lookup is indistinguishable from "nothing to do", at the level that decides whether a human ever finds out. emit_find_prs prints 'prs=' and returns 0 both when it genuinely resolved zero PRs and when it could not check at all; the workflow then guards every downstream step with `if: steps.find.outputs.prs != ''`, so both cases produce a GREEN run with the secret check and the enqueue step SKIPPED. The only difference is a NOTICE line on stderr, and `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` produces no Actions annotation, so nothing shows in the UI or the run list -- a maintainer scanning runs sees green either way. Measured above: with `gh` unavailable, rc=0, stdout 'prs=\n'. The fail-open choice is deliberate and reasoned in the docstring (the 15-minute sweep retries), and for a TRANSIENT failure I agree with it. But a PERSISTENT failure -- a revoked token scope, `gh` absent from the runner image, the repo renamed, REPO wrong -- then produces 96 green, silent, do-nothing runs a day, which is exactly the "green, looking like nothing is happening rather than like something failed" condition this workflow's own comment block was written to end, and exactly the CLAUDE.md/HANDOFF.md defect pattern "'I could not check' must never share a representation with 'I checked and found nothing'". Retry does not separate the two representations; it only shortens the transient case. Remedy without giving up fail-open: emit a second output (e.g. `resolved=false`) and one `::warning::`/`::error::` annotation on the unresolved path, so the two states stop sharing a representation while the job still does not fail.

F4 (BLOCKING, structural -- this PR cannot go green in place, whatever I concluded). reviews/44/ carries four DISAGREE records. scripts/lwb_lanes._review_ok checks `verdict` BEFORE staleness and appends a hard error for anything that is not AGREE, and check_lanes fails on any error, so a DISAGREE record cannot be cleared by adding an AGREE one. Measured: `python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 44` emits each of the four 'verdict is DISAGREE, want AGREE' FAILs nine times (once per gated commit) plus '0 independent review(s) in reviews/44/' for all nine commits. An AGREE from me would not have changed that. Note one of those four, cloud-reviewer-b-01AwCZtZW9hra7HbtgnZi72m.json, names 1f08740d -- the CURRENT reviewable head -- so it is a live DISAGREE, not a stale one. Clearing this requires deleting other reviewers' records (evidence destruction, which reviews/README.md names as falsification) or re-cutting the branch, as #46 did for #43. I make no recommendation between those; it is the author's and owner's call.

F5 (INFORMATIONAL, not blocking). proof/44.json's `commit` field is cc1189881b66ff0bebe2bfbb62919b6c9db063fb, a merge commit that modifies NEITHER deliverable file: `git log -1 --format=%H -- .github/workflows/auto-queue.yml` gives cbc66e1 and `-- scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py` gives 8630a36, and the branch has advanced to 1f08740 since. proof/schema.json defines the field only as "The commit SHA this proof record proves", which does not pin this either way, and lwb_check_proof.py --pr 44 passes, so I am NOT filing it as a violation. I flag it only because PR #46 treats this exact shape as a blocking finding (its D2), so the two PRs are being held to different standards, and because a sha in a record that no longer corresponds to anything on the branch is the staleness class this repo keeps paying for.

CONCURRENCY, considered and NOT filed. The rekeyed group falls back to `github.run_id` for the schedule sweep, so scheduled sweeps never serialize against each other or against a workflow_run run, and two runs could try to enqueue the same PR. I chased this and concluded it is not a defect worth filing: `enqueue` pins `expectedHeadOid`, so the loser is rejected by GitHub and prints a FAIL line, and that FAIL goes to main()'s stdout, which is NOT redirected into $GITHUB_OUTPUT (only the --find-prs step is). Recording it so the next reviewer does not have to re-derive it.

I did not re-verify the body's central empirical claim -- that auto-queue.yml has never fired on check_suite -- against the Actions API; I took the quoted `gh api .../runs` output on trust. I could not test any of this against real GitHub event delivery: whether `workflow_run` actually fires for both "CI" and "Handoff" as named, whether a `*/15` cron is honoured at that frequency under load, and whether `commits/{sha}/pulls` behaves as assumed for fork PRs are all unverifiable from here and remain the largest untested surface in this PR.
